incidents.what_happened: Advisor jobs had terminal failures recorded in answer.err, but the incident intake watched only node_health's six-hour successful-answer-age threshold. A red post-merge main CI run likewise had no incident path. The result was a many-hour gap between advisor failures and an issue being filed.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: A redacted captured answer.err line has the shape '[redacted-provider] ADVISOR_ANSWER_TIMEOUT: <redacted diagnostic>' (engine/mac-autopilot/fixtures/advisor-timeout-prefixed.answer.err). On origin/main, engine/providers/web-advisor-provider.sh:638-648 deleted terminal job data after returning only a raw error tail or parsed answer; engine/run-advisor-batch.sh:433-446 recorded outcome and job identity without diagnostic codes; engine/mac-autopilot/bell.sh:378-426 consumed incremental scheduler.log lines and changed alert files but never scanned advisor-batch result records. engine/mac-autopilot/node_health.py:83 marked advisor answer age unhealthy only at six hours. The same bell had a main CI run snapshot for queue handling but did not turn completed red runs into incidents.
incidents.classic_pattern: A producer discards machine-readable failure meaning before cleanup, while a downstream health aggregate observes only delayed absence of success; durable terminal events have no incident owner.
incidents.best_known_solution: Extract the three required ADVISOR_* codes and the safe picker-not-found class before provider job cleanup, persist them with each advisor batch result, and scan those results from the existing bell tick using stable #166 signatures. Use the same bell tick's main CI snapshot plus the existing bounded gh wrapper and CI test-log parser to file red-run incidents keyed by check and first test. Keep recovery quiet when a later success breaks a consecutive-failure streak.
options_considered: Lower the six-hour node-health threshold; rejected because it still waits on an aggregate symptom and cannot identify a terminal error or red CI check.
Add another polling daemon; rejected because it adds a second schedule and incident owner while the bell already owns #166 upsert and dedupe.

Capture durable advisor diagnostics and inspect advisor results plus the existing CI snapshot in one bell scan; selected because failure detection uses the event already emitted and reuses #166 hashing, severity and upsert.

siblings.expected_result: Three redacted answer.err shapes yield one issue per required signature in one scan; the planted pre-fix bell misses a timeout; isolated fail-then-success is quiet; picker fallback and red/green main CI fixtures follow the same intake.

machine_checks.why: Replays three redacted real answer.err shapes, checks pending-job diagnostics survive, verifies fail streak and recovery behavior, and exercises picker fallback plus red/green main CI incident intake.
Removes the new bell scan calls to plant the pre-fix behavior; a real redacted timeout result is missed and the guard reports the expected failure.

incidents.what_happened: Four ready-to-merge hotpatch units (release-blocker PRs on hotfix/* branches) stayed on draft PRs for hours while 5 of 12 PR runners idled; every slow tick logged merge skipped PR#<n> (draft, waiting for its CI slot) and no admission path flipped them.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Live scheduler.log 2026-11-03T05:24:24Z repeats merge skipped PR#4938/4940/4942/4921 (draft, waiting for its CI slot); the PRs carry no agent/ci-gated label, so gated_ready returned at the [[ -n "$pr" ]] || return 0 guard (engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/ci-status.sh:371 pre-fix) while the WIP selection excludes them via (.hotpatch // false) != true (engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/ci-admission.sh:156): the two selectors have an empty intersection, so no code path could ever ready them.
incidents.classic_pattern: A membership-gated handler returns success without acting (silent no-op), and the population it silently drops is excluded from every other path by a disjoint predicate: starvation with all capacity idle.
incidents.best_known_solution: A single admission decision point must resolve PR draft/head state from the full PR census when the gated-label census does not index the unit, and a symptom watch must alert when a ready-to-merge draft waits past a bound while free slots exist.
options_considered: Add the gated label to hotfix PRs at orphan adoption; this repairs one registration path but any other unlabeled draft source starves the same way.
Drop the hotpatch exclusion so hotpatches take product CI slots; this inverts the hotfix exemption design and queues hotfixes behind product CI.
Resolve draft/head from the full per-tick PR census inside gated_ready when the branch is unlabeled, keeping one ready decision point for labeled and unlabeled drafts; selected.
Add ci_slot_starve_watch so any future class of un-readable ready draft alerts within a bounded time while free slots exist; selected as the symptom guard.

siblings.discovery_command: grep -c 'draft, waiting for its CI slot' "$A/scheduler.log" vs gh api runners busy count
siblings.expected_result: Zero ready-to-merge drafts remain after an admission pass with free slots; CI-SLOT-STARVE alerts otherwise.

machine_checks.why: Replays the live four-unit unlabeled-draft population through ci_admission: all readied in one pass with 5 free slots, starvation watch alerts after three slow admission ticks with free slots and stays silent at zero free slots, and the per-pass slot_sync and product-path lookup bounds hold.
Plants the verbatim pre-fix gated_ready and proves the replay detects the un-readied drafts (fail against the real past bad code) and starts the starvation clock.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #156 used an unbalanced pattern in a jq test() filter. Fixtures reached it only when one specific history entry existed, so ordinary coverage missed the syntax error.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #156 was fixed in commit 22e253d with a scheduler regression case; the pattern can be compiled directly with jq.
incidents.classic_pattern: A data-dependent fixture leaves a literal regular expression uncompiled until one exact branch is selected.
incidents.best_known_solution: Compile every literal jq test(), match(), capture(), sub() and gsub() pattern in engine shell files with jq before relying on fixture execution.
options_considered: Add a fixture for the known history entry; this would cover one branch but leave other literal patterns dependent on fixture data.
Compile every literal regex with jq itself; this covers syntax independently of runtime data and was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Every literal jq regex in engine shell files compiles successfully.

machine_checks.why: Compiles engine literals and proves an unbalanced planted pattern is rejected.
Retains the original scheduler regression case.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157 cached candidate rows containing issue bodies by passing the complete string to jq through --arg. A large intake exceeded the OS argument limit and failed with Argument list too long.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Issue #157 was fixed in commit e4a748c by streaming the cache rows; scheduler.test.sh adds a fixture over 2 MiB.
incidents.classic_pattern: A growing list or body is bound as one jq argv value; per-argument limits can be exceeded before the program starts.
incidents.best_known_solution: Stream large JSON or prose through stdin or a file, and lint known-unbounded variable names passed to --arg or --argjson.
options_considered: Truncate issue bodies; this loses cache data and does not bound row counts.
Split the cache into multiple argv chunks; this keeps the same fragile transport contract.
Stream the serialized value to jq and flag --arg/--argjson bindings of known unbounded variables; this avoids argv limits and follows the existing lint style, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: A rows variable passed through --arg is flagged; fixed stdin streaming passes.

machine_checks.why: Proves a planted --arg rows "$rows" binding is flagged and scans production shell files.
Exercises the #159 large-row cache regression above 2 MiB.

incidents.what_happened: Issue #157's refill path read HANDOFF_PR_CENSUS before assignment under set -u, aborting a tick before existing startable work was dispatched.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The fix from branch fix/refill-census-unbound merged in pull request #160 as commit c9cb023.
incidents.classic_pattern: A fallback path skips a path-local assignment and later reads an unset variable under nounset.
incidents.best_known_solution: Initialize the census before refill or fallback reads and keep nounset enabled.
options_considered: Disable nounset for the fallback; this suppresses the useful error and lets missing state flow onward.
Initialize the census before every path can read it; this preserves nounset and gives fallback logic a defined empty state, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: Refill completes and existing startable work dispatches despite the handoff lookup path.

machine_checks.why: Regression case reaches the refill fallback with set -u and checks dispatch continues.

incidents.what_happened: One gh pr list call hung for 44 minutes until TICK-TIMEOUT; refill remained locked out for 28 minutes.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The scheduler wrapper called command gh without a timeout; the bounded-wrapper fix is on branch fix/scheduler-gh-timeout.
incidents.classic_pattern: An unbounded network CLI call can keep a scheduler lock longer than the useful work window.
incidents.best_known_solution: Route scheduler gh() through gh_timeout with a validated per-call limit, log timed-out calls, and statically reject direct command gh calls in scheduler and library sources.
options_considered: Raise TICK-TIMEOUT; this lengthens the maximum lockout rather than bounding each network call.
Retry a stalled command; without a deadline this repeats the same unbounded wait.
Use one bounded timeout wrapper for scheduler GitHub calls and fail static checks on direct command gh bypasses; this constrains each call and prevents callsite drift, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: No production scheduler/lib shell source calls command gh directly.

machine_checks.why: Checks all scheduler/lib shell sources and proves a planted command gh bypass is rejected.
Times out a stalled gh CLI call, verifies the child is stopped, and checks timeout logging.

incidents.what_happened: A product-pin rollback was refused by publish preflight with resolved-config-check: CHANGED, leaving a broken engine live.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: The preflight did not recognize the explicit rollback path; the engine-swap canary fix is on branch feat/engine-swap-canary.
incidents.classic_pattern: A broad safety preflight blocks a narrowly authorized recovery change because the recovery path is not modeled as an allowed transition.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep ordinary changed-config checks, while allowing only an explicit verified engine-swap/canary path to carry the product pin change.
options_considered: Skip preflight for every rollback; this would permit unrelated resolved-config drift.
Leave the old engine live until a fresh forward release is ready; this prolongs a known-broken state.
Require a verified engine-swap path for the pin change while preserving ordinary refusal behavior; this keeps the gate and supports controlled recovery, so it was selected.

siblings.expected_result: The verified swap/rollback case passes while unlisted resolved-config changes remain blocked.

machine_checks.why: Exercises engine version selection and publish preflight behavior.
Keeps the default refusal for unlisted resolved-config changes and accepts listed changes with a reason.

incidents.class: optional file reads confused with persistence loss
incidents.what_happened: Intake parsed a missing per-issue JSON file while checking for an optional scheduler handoff. jqf captured jq stderr and logged the missing-file error on every candidate pass, even though the caller redirected stderr and no handoff was expected.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/intake.sh read the candidate state path through jqf without an existence-aware optional-file reader; the runtime scheduler log shows repeated missing-file diagnostics for open ready-for-agent issues. engine/lib.d/issue-state.sh creates per-issue JSON lazily through state_merge and issue_transition, and the repository has no general cleanup for those JSON files.
incidents.classic_pattern: An optional input reaches a parser before absence is modeled, so normal absence is reported as an error and repeated at the call site.
options_considered: Suppress jqf logging globally for missing paths; rejected because missing required inputs would lose their diagnostics.
Add existence checks only at intake call sites; rejected because the same optional-file pattern appears in shared scheduler caches and a check followed by a separate read can race.

Add jqf_optional_file in the shared scheduler core, return a distinct status for true absence, and keep existing paths on jqf; chosen because callers can model absence while malformed and unreadable files remain diagnostic.
incidents.best_known_solution: Route optional scheduler file reads through jqf_optional_file. It returns status 64 without logging only when a path is absent; callers treat that status as an empty optional value, and existing paths still use jqf so parse and read failures are logged.

incidents.what_happened: Every pipeline tick since 2026-11-03 05:23Z was refused: one advisor batch member had a live scheduler worker, pipeline_batch_claim_acquire returned 1, the advisor stage translated it to exit 75, and issue-pipeline-slices.sh counted only 0/124/137 as non-failures, so failed=1 and run-tick refused the tick. The same batch re-triaged two tickets whose scheduler units were in flight, which is what made a member busy in the first place.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/issue-pipeline-slices.sh slice case (pre-fix: '0) ;; 124|137) ... *) failed=1') had no defer arm; engine/issue-pipeline.sh dispatch_advisor_batch claim-unavailable 'return 75'; live journal shows repeated 'run-tick: refusing to run this tick — issue-pipeline.sh exited with status 1' and the live autopilot scheduler.log shows the incident signature matched nothing in engine/mac-autopilot/bell.sh scheduler_signature_class().
incidents.classic_pattern: A component communicates 'temporary, retry later' through a non-zero exit code that an aggregator treats as failure, so a single soft miss is escalated to a whole-system outage; paired with a monitor that only recognizes hard-crash signatures, the outage also files no incident.
incidents.best_known_solution: Make the defer contract explicit in one place (ZF_SLICE_DEFER_STATUS in engine/issue-pipeline-slices.sh): slices treat 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) as defer-and-continue like an overrun; batch claims drop busy members instead of refusing the batch; selection never re-triages an issue with an in-flight scheduler unit; the refusal and the failing slice append a stable signature line to the scheduler log the bell scans.
options_considered: Map every non-zero slice status to success; rejected because real stage failures (exit 1) must still refuse the tick.
Catch 75 at each dispatch call site only; rejected because the stage-exit contract stays implicit and the next defer-producing path re-triggers the outage.
One named defer status honored by the slice runner, with busy batch members dropped instead of refusing the batch; selected: the contract is declared once and every producer of 75 is covered.

siblings.expected_result: Slice-contract, batch-claim and in-flight-triage guards all pass; each case fails on the pre-fix engine.

machine_checks.why: Exercises the real slice runner with exit 75/1, the real batch claim with one busy member, and the in-flight triage skip against rereview/ready-to-merge unit fixtures.

incidents.what_happened: Most intake ticks logged 'jqf error (rc=2) in intake_candidates: jq: error: writing output failed: Broken pipe' (69 lines in the live scheduler.log, 2026-10-30 through 2026-11-03, latest 04:01:33Z) and dispatch_supervisor_arbiters the same (16 lines). Consumers stop reading jqf streams early by design - register_new_issues breaks at 'added < want', arbiter dispatch returns at capacity, 'jqf | head -n' bounds rows - and under systemd (SIGPIPE ignored) jq reports the closed pipe as rc=2 with that message, so jqf logged a healthy truncation as an error and buried real ones in scheduler.log, the incident intake and the canary signature baseline (extract_signatures normalizes every jqf error line).
incidents.root_cause_evidence: engine/mac-autopilot/scheduler.d/core.sh jqf() logged every non-zero jq exit whose stderr was non-empty; intake.sh:289 '(( added < want )) || break' closes the candidate stream fed at intake.sh:574 while the producer's jqf is still writing; evals-arbiter.sh dispatch_supervisor_arbiters returns 0 from inside a loop fed by 'done < <(jqf ... "$UNITS")' (evals-arbiter.sh:355). With SIGPIPE ignored (systemd service, command substitution) jq exits 2 with 'jq: error: writing output failed: Broken pipe'; with SIGPIPE default it dies silently with rc=141 and empty stderr, which jqf already did not log.
incidents.classic_pattern: A producer wrapper reports every downstream failure as its own error, so a consumer that stops reading by design (break, return, head) is indistinguishable from a real processing failure in the logs, and the noise hides genuine errors from humans and signature scanners.
incidents.best_known_solution: jqf treats exactly 'writing output failed: Broken pipe' (EPIPE on jq's stdout, only possible when the downstream reader closed) as not an error and skips the log line; every other first-line message - parse and runtime errors, and write failures such as ENOSPC - is still logged. jq's exit code is returned unchanged. One fix in the shared wrapper covers all ~50 'done < <(jqf ...)' consumers; no per-consumer draining.
options_considered: Suppress every rc=2 write failure; rejected because ENOSPC and other real output failures share the exit code.
Drain or bound the candidate stream in intake instead; rejected because it fixes one consumer of ~50 with the same shape and keeps the wrapper lying about the class.
Skip the log line only for the exact EPIPE message; selected: EPIPE on stdout can only mean the consumer closed the pipe, so the carve-out cannot hide a real jq failure.

siblings.expected_result: Early-stopping consumers log no jqf error and real failures still do; every case fails on the pre-fix wrapper (exit 1 on origin/main).

machine_checks.why: Runs the real jqf wrapper with a bounded 'jqf | head' consumer, a read loop that breaks early, a malformed-JSON parse error and an ENOSPC write to /dev/full; the first two must stay silent, the last two must log.
Adjacent contract on the same wrapper: real malformed-state jq failures through register_new_issues keep their jqf diagnostics.

incidents.what_happened: The per-unit advisor launched Node with a bundled provider path based on the engine-live symlink's parent. Node returned MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the unit fell back to arbiter review.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original log: Error: Cannot find module '<engine-live>/../.agents/skills/web-advisor-provider/ask.cjs' (MODULE_NOT_FOUND). engine/config.sh:45 kept ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical for live-link behavior, while :112 derived the provider path by appending ../ to that logical path. The planted case in engine/config.test.sh fails on the old derivation.
incidents.classic_pattern: A logical symlink path is used to find a sibling resource with .., so lookup follows the symlink's parent instead of the directory containing the target version.
incidents.best_known_solution: Keep ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical for live-link reload behavior, resolve its physical directory once in engine/config.sh, and derive every parent-relative path from that physical parent. Before launching a unit advisor, require a readable provider; log one stable scheduler line, route to arbiter review, and let the bell file the incident through issue upsert.
options_considered: Make ZF_ENGINE_DIR physical everywhere; this fixes sibling lookup but changes the logical live-link path used by long-running loops after a swap.
Resolve only the provider script at its caller; this leaves ZF_REPO_DIR and any other parent-relative engine defaults exposed to the same symlink error.
Keep ZF_ENGINE_DIR logical and derive one physical parent in config.sh for all parent-relative defaults; selected because it fixes the whole path family while preserving live-link behavior.

siblings.expected_result: The planted engine-live symlink resolves the provider script into the physical version root; the old derivation exits 1 with a path mismatch.

machine_checks.why: Sources config.sh through a symlinked engine with ZF_ENGINE_DIR unset and asserts the provider script resolves inside the physical version root.
Proves an absent provider is routed to arbiter review without launching the advisor, logs one diagnostic, and files one bell incident through the issue-upsert entry point.

incidents.what_happened: A review was configured on gpt-6-luna max, matching the Codex/Luna family that wrote the head. The old resolver returned the implementer's identity whenever its different-provider review role was unavailable, so the verifier could be the same family as the worker it reviewed.
incidents.root_cause_evidence: Original journal line: 'run-tick: <agent-state> fast-forwarded to origin/main, now at: [skip ci] config(models): review runs on gpt-6-luna max, matching the model policy; handing off to issue-pipeline.sh'. The pre-fix engine/lib.d/model-policy.sh:761 printed implement_identity after the cross-provider role was unavailable, making the configured matching family an accepted verifier.
incidents.classic_pattern: A fail-open availability fallback reuses the identity being checked, so a verification control loses independence exactly when its preferred verifier is unavailable. Shared model-family failures then affect both the change and its review.
incidents.best_known_solution: Classify identities in one model-family table and select a reviewer using the model/backend recorded on the unit or its latest implement/repair worker. Codex heads try GLM, then a policy-authorized Sonnet review_fallback; GLM heads try Codex, then Sonnet. Reject same-family candidates and keep the review pending with one #166 bell intake line when all independent reviewers are unavailable.
options_considered: Use a different Codex model such as Terra when Luna is the author; rejected because model changes inside Codex remain the same model family.
Return to the author's identity when GLM is unavailable; rejected because the reviewer loses independence during the exact outage this fallback handles.
Use the cross-family reviewer first, allow Sonnet only for the named review_fallback role, then wait and alert; selected because no unavailable-provider path can dispatch the author's family.

siblings.expected_result: The planted pre-fix resolver exits 1 after dispatching gpt-6-luna for its same-family bad config; the fixed dispatcher refuses that config and the full focused guard exits 0.

machine_checks.why: Routes Luna-authored work to GLM and GLM-authored work to Luna, refuses a planted same-family config, tests Sonnet fallback and both-held wait/alert, checks Claude remains forbidden for implement, and requires the planted historical fail-open selector to fail with same-family dispatch evidence.
